summary: seo-gap-miner 0.2.0 performs its grounded review during the initial governed run, records a review act, and was dogfooded against public Google Trends and NBA evidence.

package.name: seo-gap-miner
package.publish_method: runx login --provider github --for publish; runx registry publish ./skills/seo-gap-miner --registry https://api.runx.ai --version 0.2.0

observations: The registry publish succeeded only after hosted runx reconstructed the package and reran its publish harness.
A clean registry install resolved version 0.2.0 with the expected package and profile digests.
The local harness passed 3/3: grounded-content-gaps-sealed, thin-demand-needs-more-evidence, and missing-input-needs-agent.
No caller answers or runx resume step are present; run.mjs performs the judgment in the analyze graph step.
The top-level graph declares form review, and the post-publish dogfood receipt contains act_turn with form review and a closed seal.
Every emitted finding names runx/draft-content as the downstream lane.
The real dogfood input records the official Google Trends US Trending Now RSS URL, retrieval timestamp, RSS SHA-256, and public NBA page URLs.
Google Trends reported approximate traffic of 500+ for both Cameron Carr and Lakers Summer League; the runner returned two weak-page findings grounded in the bounded NBA inventory.
Plain runx verify succeeded in production mode with valid digest, content address, and Ed25519 signature.

dogfood.command: runx skill gebibd00-jpg/seo-gap-miner@0.2.0 --registry https://api.runx.ai -i site_ref=https://www.nba.com/ --input-json site_inventory=<json> --input-json demand_fixtures=<json> --input-json content_policy=<json> --json
